task.title: Configuring Red Hat Quay to use AWS STS
task.shortdesc: To configure Red Hat Quay to use AWS STS for Amazon S3 storage, you can update the DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG block in your config.yaml file and restart the registry.

step.cmd: Update your config.yaml file for Red Hat Quay to include the following information:

info.codeblock: # ... DISTRIBUTED_STORAGE_CONFIG: default: - STSS3Storage - sts_role_arn: <role_arn> s3_bucket: <s3_bucket_name> storage_path: <storage_path> s3_region: <region> sts_user_access_key: <s3_user_access_key> sts_user_secret_key: <s3_user_secret_key> # ...

dlentry.dd: Specifies the unique Amazon Resource Name (ARN) required when configuring AWS STS.
Specifies the name of your S3 bucket.
Specifies the storage path for data. Usually /datastorage.
Specifies the Amazon Web Services region. Defaults to us-east-1.
Specifies the generated AWS S3 user access key required when configuring AWS STS.
Specifies the generated AWS S3 user secret key required when configuring AWS STS.

step.cmd: Restart your Red Hat Quay deployment.

ol.li: Tag a sample image, for example, busybox, that you push to the repository. For example: $ podman tag docker.io/library/busybox <quay-server.example.com>/<organization_name>/busybox:test
Push the sample image by running the following command: $ podman push <quay-server.example.com>/<organization_name>/busybox:test
Verify that the push was successful by navigating to the Organization that you pushed the image to in your Red Hat Quay registry → Tags.
Navigate to the Amazon Web Services (AWS) console and locate your S3 bucket.
Click the name of your S3 bucket.
On the Objects page, click datastorage/.

On the datastorage/ page, the following resources should appear:
sha256/
uploads/
These resources indicate that the push was successful, and that AWS STS is properly configured.
